justification: Notification-delivery fix for two interest-capture routes (DCP tab 'Notify me' and Verify registration). Two defects: (1) both sent from onboarding@resend.dev, Resend's test sender that only delivers to the account owner; (2) both sent to info@plotdetect.com.au while also sending from info@plotdetect.com.au — a self-domain send via an external relay that Google Workspace quarantines as spoofing (Resend shows 'delivered' but the mailbox never receives it, confirmed live). Switched the sender to the verified info@plotdetect.com.au domain, and routed the recipient to an off-domain NOTIFY_EMAIL (env-overridable, default lawrence.mcdonell@gmail.com) so From != To and Workspace accepts it. Guarded dcp-interest on RESEND_API_KEY for parity. No DB or data-path change.
functions: N/A - no functions added, changed, or removed; a string literal changed and an existing send call was wrapped in an env-var guard.
values: N/A - no DB or API values read or written by this change; the INSERT path and its parameters are untouched.
queries: N/A - no database queries added or modified.

break_it.scenario: Notification still routed to an @plotdetect.com.au address, re-triggering the Google Workspace self-domain spoofing quarantine so the mailbox never receives it despite a 'delivered' status.
break_it.what_happens: Resend reports delivered but the email is silently quarantined by Workspace; the operator never sees the registration alert.
break_it.how: Recipient moved off-domain to NOTIFY_EMAIL (default lawrence.mcdonell@gmail.com), so From (info@plotdetect.com.au) != To; a foreign-domain recipient only checks SPF/DKIM, which pass, as proven by canibuildit confirmations already landing at gmail.com. If NOTIFY_EMAIL is later set back to an @plotdetect.com.au address the bug returns, which the code comment warns against.
break_it.repro: Submit the DCP tab 'Notify me' form on a preview with RESEND_API_KEY set and confirm a 'DCP interest' email lands in the NOTIFY_EMAIL Gmail inbox; contrast with the pre-fix info@ send that showed delivered but never arrived.

break_it.scenario: RESEND_API_KEY is unset in the environment, so constructing the Resend client throws and breaks the request.
break_it.what_happens: Previously dcp-interest called new Resend(undefined) unconditionally; if the key is absent the send rejects. The registration still saves because the send is fire-and-forget, but the code path is fragile.
break_it.how: dcp-interest is now wrapped in if (process.env.RESEND_API_KEY) like verify-interest, so the send is skipped cleanly when the key is absent and the INSERT/200 path is unaffected.
break_it.repro: Unset RESEND_API_KEY locally, POST to /api/dcp-interest, and confirm the row inserts and the route returns 200 with no thrown error.

post_merge.db_reset: Not required - no schema or data changes; dcp_interest and verify_interest tables and their INSERT paths are untouched.
post_merge.secrets: No new secrets; relies on the existing RESEND_API_KEY already configured for the six other email routes. Verify it is present in the frontend Vercel project env.
post_merge.other_repo: No coupling to other repos or deploys; frontend-only change deployed via Vercel.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - on the Vercel preview with RESEND_API_KEY set, submit the DCP tab 'Notify me' form for an unprocessed council and confirm a 'DCP interest' email arrives at info@plotdetect.com.au; repeat via the Verify registration prompt.
